jobDescription: We build a product-analytics platform that mobile app companies use to run A/B tests. The Data Scientist on the experimentation team designs the statistical methods behind the platform's test reports, reviews customer experiments that look anomalous, writes methodology notes for the public documentation site and supports the solutions engineers on technical customer calls. The team asks for at least five years of applied data science work that includes controlled experiments, and for a working knowledge of sequential testing. The team is four data scientists who report to the head of statistics.
requirements: Designs and validates statistical methods for A/B test reporting, including variance reduction.
Has working knowledge of sequential testing and can explain stopping rules to customers.
Has at least five years of applied data science experience that includes controlled experiments.
Writes methodology notes for the public documentation site.
Supports solutions engineers on technical customer calls about experiment results.

evidence.text: Data Scientist, Hartwell Apps (July 2022 to August 2026): implemented CUPED variance reduction in the in-house experiment reporting service and validated it with A/A simulations on twelve months of historical tests.

Wrote the internal guide to the mixture sequential probability ratio test used by Hartwell's experimentation dashboard, with worked examples of when a test may stop early and when it must run to its planned horizon.

Data Scientist, Corbel Software (January 2019 to June 2022): analysed pricing-page and onboarding experiments for a subscription product and reported the results to the growth team at the end of each sprint.
Answered statistics questions from internal product managers in a weekly office hour and reviewed the analysis plan for each new experiment before launch.
Education: BSc Mathematics, University of Dunmere (2018).

Work sample: a published methodology note from Hartwell's developer blog explaining how the experiment dashboard computes confidence intervals with CUPED, including the A/A simulation chart and the code snippet that generated it.

HR verification note: employment dates were confirmed in writing by the HR departments of Corbel Software and Hartwell Apps; the confirmed periods give seven years and eight months in all as a data scientist working on product experiments.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate can start after a four-week notice period and asked whether the solutions engineers' customer calls take place in European time zones.

propositions.text: The candidate has seven years and eight months of employer-confirmed data science experience on product experiments, which meets the five-year requirement.
propositions.rationale: Both employers confirmed the periods in writing and the HR verification note states the total; the resume entries describe experiment work in both roles.

propositions.text: The candidate implemented CUPED variance reduction in an experiment reporting service and validated it with A/A simulations.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the work and the published methodology note shows the method and the A/A simulation.

propositions.rationale: The resume describes the guide and its contents directly.
